author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: Being undesirable, that image is misshapen.
context_before: Remember the day your boss criticized you, and you are molding an image of yourself based upon what he said.
context_after: Unable to discard yourself, go down to the potter’s house by taking the same scene and reshaping yourself by remembering the day your boss congratulated you on your accomplishments. Will this act change your world? Yes! I tell you: the God of the universe is shaping you morning, noon, and night, as you accept words, actions, and events from seeming others.

quote_original: Then believe you are the Lord!
context_before: You are not someone apart from God, for I AM cannot be divided. The Lord, our God, is one I AM, not two! If God’s I AM and your I AM is the same I AM, define what you would like to be.
context_after: Be like the lady who transformed a streetcar into a cruise. Lose yourself in your new state, while your world on the outside remains, momentarily, the same.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Imagining Creates (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: I tell you: imagining creates reality!
context_before: person who has been unfaithful and you enjoy a bit of gossip. All of these are ideas implanted in the mind, which cause the rise and fall of nations.
context_after: If you want to change your life you must become aware of the ideas you are planting in the mind of others! When you meet someone who is negative, put a lovely idea in its place. Then, whenever you think of him, imagine he is telling you something lovely. And, because you now walk in a world that is not disturbed by his negative state, when he finds himself no longer thinking negative thoughts, he will never know you were its source. You will know it and that is all that is important.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Imagining Creates (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: The Bible tells the same story.
context_before: I saw a monstrous witch in a cave teaching little children the black arts. When she saw me she screamed: “O Man of God, what have you to do with me?”
context_after: Those who teach the black arts and how to hurt people, those who would control your mind and make you dependent upon them, are only personifications of organizations who keep you from contacting the only God who is within you. Every orthodox religious group would enslave you for the rest of eternity if they could; but when you leave that belief, its personification will curse your leaving, but their curse means nothing. They cannot touch you when you completely reject any intermediary between yourself and God.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Imagining Creates (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Are you imagining you are secure now?
context_before: When you imagined being secure did you forget the feeling?
context_after: You may have no evidence that you are secure, but as you allow others to tell you how much you are loved and wanted, how successful and famous you are, you will begin to assume it, and imagination will have created its reality. Try it, for that reality you already are!
